title: Audit Objection Giving a New Opinion, Not New Evidence, Cannot Justify Reopening a Completed Assessment: Sikkim High Court
case_name: Zydus Healthcare Limited v. Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Circle 3(2), Gangtok & Ors.
citation: WP(C) Nos. 39 of 2022, 13 of 2024 and 50 of 2025
card_summary: The Sikkim High Court quashed reassessment notices against Zydus Healthcare for three years, holding that an audit objection stating a different opinion on an issue already examined is not new evidence. Justice Bhaskar Raj Pradhan held Section 149(1)(b) needs new evidence, not a new opinion, so the revenue could not reopen assessments on a Rs 22.99 crore excise refund treated as capital receipt.
card_tip: Before accepting a reopening notice founded on an audit objection, check whether it points to fresh material or just disagrees with a view the assessing officer already took; the latter will not survive a challenge.
verification_notes: Decision date (14 October 2026) and the three WP numbers are consistent across LiveLawBiz and Taxscan. Both sources agree on the judge, the Section 149(1)(b) reasoning, and the excise-duty/goodwill subject matter. Neither source gave a neutral citation for the judgment itself, so none is stated.
